Gold.note: Central bank buying and rate cut expectations support prices despite extended levels.

Silver.note: Strong solar panel demand and monetary premium drive a structural market deficit.

Copper.note: Tight concentrate markets and electrification demand outweigh sluggish Chinese property sector.

Uranium.note: Structural supply deficit from mine closures and robust nuclear demand from AI data centers.

Lithium.note: Persistent oversupply and slowing EV growth rates continue to pressure producer margins.

Nickel.note: Massive Indonesian supply growth and LFP battery substitution weigh heavily on prices.

Zinc.note: Smelter treatment charge collapses and mine closures tighten refined supply availability.

Iron Ore.note: Weak Chinese property sector and high seaborne supply limit upside potential.

Coal.note: Ample global inventories and long-term thermal coal demand destruction cap upside.

Rare Earths.note: Weak traditional auto demand and ample Chinese supply keep prices depressed.

Manganese.note: Steady steel demand and emerging battery applications provide a stable price floor.

PGM.note: Substitution of platinum for palladium and weak auto production limit near-term upside.

Potash.note: Resilient global agricultural demand and normalized supply chains support steady pricing.

Aluminum.note: Chinese production capacity caps and strong green energy demand tighten the market.

Diversified.note: Balanced exposure to copper and iron ore provides a hedge against single-commodity volatility.
